methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in AI & Software. Range: $3.8B - $8.3B.

public.rationale: Public-co frontier-tech comp in AI & Compute

data.narrative:
Applied Intuition, a Series F AI & Software company founded by Qasar Younis and Peter Ludwig, has raised over $600M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of 3 same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Together AI (Series G, $8.3B), SandboxAQ (Series E, $5.8B), and Ayar Labs (Series E, $3.8B)—supplemented by a broader universe of 9 private frontier-tech companies and 1 public comparable (Palantir).

Stage-progression methodology was not applicable; the stated $15B last post-money valuation implies a multiple of 25x total capital raised, indicating a data-quality issue with that input. The peer-median approach is the primary triangulation method, anchoring the analysis. The three direct comparables yield a median valuation of $5.8B, with a range spanning $3.8B to $8.3B.

This analysis supports a valuation range of $4.9B (low) to $6.6B (high), centered at $5.8B. The median reflects Applied Intuition's position within the AI & Software peer cohort at similar or slightly more advanced funding stages. Key uncertainties include the company's revenue scale relative to peers, customer concentration, and near-term path to profitability—factors not captured in stage-based comparables alone. The tight peer set size (n=3) limits precision; expansion to the broader private frontier-tech universe would improve confidence in range boundaries.
